To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

swimming exercise training improves blood pressure and insulin resistance in young patients with essential hypertension, and that the effects are greater in patients with higher baseline values of insulin resistance.
swimming training is effective in improving blood pressure and insulin resistance in hypertensive patients.
1-year aerobic swimming exercise can significantly reduce blood pressure and improve insulin sensitivity in mild hypertension young patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of one-year swimming on blood pressure and metabolic parameters in mild hypertensive subjects.
the effects of swimming exercise on the cardiovascular and metabolic parameters of mild hypertensive young subjects.
the effects of swimming training on blood lipid profile, insulin sensitivity and blood pressure in mild hypertensive patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

swimming training is effective for the treatment of hypertension in the general population, and it is also effective for the treatment in hypertensive patients with diabetes mellitus and in hypertensive patients without diabetes mellitus.
swimming training is a safe and effective way of improving cardiovascular health, including blood pressure, in hypertensive patients.
swimming is an effective exercise modality for reducing blood pressure and improving insulin resistance in young hypertensive patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the swimming training in mild hypertensive patients improves blood pressure, insulin sensitivity, and body mass index (BMI), without any change in heart rate.
one year of swimming training is an effective way to improve blood pressure control and insulin sensitivity in patients with mild hypertension.
swimming training is a safe and efficient way to improve insulin sensitivity in young hypertensive patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of exercise training on insulin sensitivity and glucose tolerance in hypertensive patients may be mediated by a reduction of blood pressure.
swimming training is effective to reduce blood pressure in young patients with mild hypertension.
the effect of exercise training on the blood pressure of patients with essential hypertension is dependent on baseline blood pressure.
